1.s: A family tree from Adam through Noah and Abraham to Esau’s descendants.
1.d: The Chronicler begins by showing Israel’s place among the nations, tracing its ancestry from Adam to Jacob with information from Genesis [[tosn:1 Chronicles 1:1–2:2]].

2.s: The sons of Israel (Jacob), and the line of Judah leading to David.
2.d: Judah’s genealogy is the most detailed, with background on David’s ancestors [[tosn:1 Chronicles 2:3–8]]. The lists begin with Judah, David’s tribe [[tosn:1 Chronicles 8:1–40]].

3.s: David’s sons and the kings of Judah, continuing past the exile to Zerubbabel and beyond.
3.d: David’s line is traced to the sixth generation after the exile, which points to a date around 400 BC for the book [[tbd:003:Chronicles, Books of First and Second]].

4.s: More families of Judah, including Jabez, who prayed to be blessed, and the tribe of Simeon.
4.d: His mother named him Jabez “because I bore him with sorrow” [[bible:1 Chronicles 4:9]], and the Chronicler pauses the list to explain the name [[tosn:1 Chronicles 4:9–10]]. His prayer is in 4:10 [[bible:1 Chronicles 4:10]].

5.s: The tribes east of the Jordan: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, and their exile by Assyria.
5.d: Tiglath-pileser of Assyria (744–727 BC) took these tribes captive [[tosn:1 Chronicles 5:6]]; their permanent exile came from unfaithfulness [[tosn:1 Chronicles 5:25–26]], as Judah’s later did [[tosn:1 Chronicles 9:1]].

6.s: The tribe of Levi: the high priests, the temple singers Heman, Asaph and Ethan, and the Levites’ towns.
6.d: The chapter lists the high priests, the three Levite clans and the lead singers from each clan [[tosn:1 Chronicles 6:1–48]] [[tosn:1 Chronicles 6:31–47]]. Asaph’s name stands in many psalm titles [[bible:Psalm 50]] [[bible:Psalm 73]].

7.s: The tribes of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher.
7.d: Ephraim’s line ends with Joshua, son of Nun, who led Israel into the promised land [[tosn:1 Chronicles 7:20–27]].

8.s: The family of Benjamin, leading to Saul.
8.d: The lists begin with Judah, David’s tribe, and end with Benjamin, Saul’s tribe [[tosn:1 Chronicles 8:1–40]], closing with Saul’s family tree [[tosn:1 Chronicles 8:33–40]].

9.s: The people who returned from exile to Jerusalem, especially priests and Levites, and Saul’s family again.
9.d: The returned exiles are connected with the past, with priests and Levites at the centre [[tosn:1 Chronicles 9:1–34]]. The family lines stop around 538 BC, when Cyrus let the Jews return [[bsn:1 Chronicles 1:1–9:34]].

10.s: Saul dies in battle on Mount Gilboa because he was unfaithful and consulted a medium.
10.d: The Chronicler gives the reason directly: Saul died for his unfaithfulness and for consulting a medium [[bible:1 Chronicles 10:13-14]].

11.s: All Israel makes David king at Hebron. He takes Jerusalem, and his mighty men are listed.
11.d: The Chronicler skips David’s seven and a half years over Judah alone and goes straight to his rule over all Israel [[tosn:1 Chronicles 11:1–3]].

12.s: The warriors from every tribe who came to David, “with a perfect heart”, and the feast at Hebron.
12.d: Support for David began while Saul was still king, and even Saul’s relatives joined him [[tosn:1 Chronicles 12:1–22]]. All came “with a perfect heart” to make him king [[bible:1 Chronicles 12:38]].

13.s: David tries to bring the ark to Jerusalem; Uzzah dies touching it, and the ark stays with Obed-Edom.
13.d: These chapters show Jerusalem becoming Israel’s political and religious centre [[tosn:1 Chronicles 13:1–17:27]]. Touching the ark violated its holiness [[tosn:1 Chronicles 13:9–11]].

14.s: David’s house is built, his family grows, and he defeats the Philistines.
14.d: Once David ruled all Israel, the Philistines attacked [[tosn:1 Chronicles 14:8–17]]. Chronicles tells of times David was faithful and leaves some of his failures to 2 Samuel [[bsn:1 Chronicles 9:35–20:8]].

15.s: The Levites carry the ark properly to Jerusalem with singing and instruments.
15.d: The first attempt failed because it did not follow God’s instructions; this time the Levites carry the ark [[tosn:1 Chronicles 15:1–3]] [[bible:1 Chronicles 15:13]].

16.s: David appoints Levites to lead worship, and Asaph’s choir sings a psalm of thanks.
16.d: The song combines Psalm 105:1–15, Psalm 96 and Psalm 106:1, 47–48 [[tosn:1 Chronicles 16:7–36]]. “Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good” [[bible:1 Chronicles 16:34]].

17.s: God promises David a house: a son whose throne will be established forever.
17.d: Where 2 Samuel 7:14 warns that God will discipline David’s son, Chronicles keeps only the promise of steadfast love [[bible:2 Samuel 7:14]] [[bible:1 Chronicles 17:13]]. The Chronicler applies the promise to Solomon in particular [[tosn:1 Chronicles 17:13]] [[tosn:1 Chronicles 17:14]].

18.d: “He executed justice and righteousness for all his people” [[bible:1 Chronicles 18:14]].

19.s: The Ammonites insult David’s envoys, and war with Ammon and Aram follows.

20.s: David’s victory over Ammon, and battles with Philistine giants.
20.d: This war happened during David’s sin with Bathsheba, which the Chronicler does not mention [[tosn:1 Chronicles 20:1–3]].

21.s: Satan incites David to take a census; a plague follows, and David buys the threshing floor of Ornan for an altar.
21.d: 2 Samuel 24:1 says the LORD incited David; the Chronicler names Satan, the adversary [[tosn:1 Chronicles 21:1]]. His version prepares for the altar and the temple [[tosn:1 Chronicles 21:1–22:1]].

22.s: David gathers materials for the temple and charges Solomon to build it.
22.d: David could not build the temple because he had shed much blood, though his wars were not wrong [[tosn:1 Chronicles 22:8]]. Solomon was a man of peace [[tosn:1 Chronicles 22:9–10]] [[bible:1 Chronicles 22:9]].

23.s: David makes Solomon king and organizes the Levites.
23.d: The Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle [[bible:1 Chronicles 23:26]].

24.s: The priests are organized into twenty-four divisions.
24.d: The twenty-four divisions stayed the same for generations; the division of Abijah appears in Luke 1:5 [[tosn:1 Chronicles 24:7–18]] [[bible:Luke 1:5]].

25.s: The temple musicians are organized into twenty-four groups.
25.d: The musicians were set apart “to prophesy with harps, with stringed instruments, and with cymbals” [[bible:1 Chronicles 25:1]].

26.d: David’s plans for the temple were well ordered, and some Levites served on the east side of the Jordan, others on the west [[bsn:1 Chronicles 23:1–29:30]] [[bible:1 Chronicles 26:30-32]].

27.s: Army divisions, tribal leaders and royal officials.
27.d: The army served the king in divisions of 24,000, each on duty for one month of the year [[bible:1 Chronicles 27:1]].

28.s: David gives Solomon the plans for the temple “by the Spirit”, and urges him to serve God “with a perfect heart and with a willing mind”.
28.d: God gave David the temple plans by inspiration, as he gave the plans for the tabernacle and for Ezekiel’s temple [[tosn:1 Chronicles 28:11–21]] [[bible:Exodus 25:9]].

29.s: The people give willingly for the temple. David prays, “All things come from you, and we have given you of your own.” Solomon is made king, and David dies.
29.d: David’s prayer praises God’s power, dedicates the offerings and asks for faithful hearts [[tosn:1 Chronicles 29:10–19]]: “all things come from you, and we have given you of your own” [[bible:1 Chronicles 29:14]].
